semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL clause 'There are three region in this diagram' is quoted from the requirement and preserved as an exact quotation; it maps to a cardinality contract on ActiveState's concurrent-region domain (CARD-BIND-NL1, required=3). The exact source inventory (llms_emp_feedback_final_0037.puml lines 5,9,10,16,17,23,24 and the resolved state refs for FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion, Inactive, and the three Collision leaf states) establishes that ActiveState has no canonical '--' orthogonal-region separators, so the primary structural reading yields 1 implicit region rather than 3 -- an established violation of the exact required cardinality. However, a second competent reading remains open on these same exact facts: the three sub-states named '...CollisionRegion' (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) could themselves be read as informally naming three separate region-like partitions intended by the author, even though they are not formally separated by UML region syntax. This is a genuine undercutting alternative because it is compatible with the same closed containment facts (the three '...Region' named children coexist with Inactive and the three Collision leaf states as siblings) and does not require any additional unsupported predicate -- it is a second semantic reading of the same exact structural inventory, not a rebuttal that satisfies the cardinality property. Because the frozen registry lacks a dedicated region-partition predicate (predicate_id=null, backend=none, verdict=unknown), this predicate/backend unavailability is a W-boundary matter only and does not itself decide between the two readings; per the cardinality protocol, when two competent scope/member readings remain compatible with the same finite inventory, the correct disposition is established-with-surviving-undercutting-defeater rather than unresolved.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: An alternative reading in which the three sibling children explicitly named 'FrontendCollisionRegion', 'RearEndCollisionRegion', and 'PedestrianCollisionRegion' (source lines 9, 14, 19) are treated by the author as the intended three regions of ActiveState, even absent canonical UML '--' orthogonal-region separator syntax; this reading is compatible with the same exact closed containment inventory supplied in the dossier and is therefore a competent second structural reading, not a mere conceivable possibility.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL requirement 'There are three region in this diagram' (NL-CONTRACT-NL1-DERIVED-7ea3476996b445b07b22) requires ActiveState to realize 3 canonical UML concurrent regions, but the closed source inventory shows ActiveState's direct children (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion, Inactive, FrontendCollision, RearEndCollision, PedestrianCollision at lines 9,14,19,24,25,26,27) contain no exact '--' separator-derived region partitioning, so under the primary canonical-region reading ActiveState realizes only 1 implicit region, not 3.

response.reason: This lens compares the NL contracts against the exact author-source inventory and closed FCSTM structure to find omitted/collapsed contracts, containment/owner default-entry defects, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, and unauthorized edges. Key findings: (1) NL-CONTRACT-REF-003 requires Inactive->active-mode transition on any of three collision events, but the closed FCSTM instead routes Inactive to three distinct leaf sub-states (FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision) that are dead-end leaves with no path back into the orthogonal regions, so the group's alternatives never reach the composite target that structurally owns the concurrent regions; (2) the FrontendCollisionRegion/RearEndCollisionRegion/PedestrianCollisionRegion composites (which host the three concurrent regions required by NL1/NL3) have no author-authorized entry edge from Inactive or from ActiveState's default entry -- ActiveState's own default entry targets only Inactive, and the three collision leaf states have no outgoing edge into the region composites at all, so the composites that own the "orthogonal regions" behavior lack any reachable owner-local default entry; (3) the guard-disjointness group ALT-NL2-1/2/3 selects distinct non-overlapping events (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian) so alternatives are not guard-colliding -- however the real structural defect is that none of the three alternatives target the required "active mode" region composites, they target isolated leaf placeholders instead (wrong_target).

additional_contracts.basis: exact_source_inventory transitions tr_0003/tr_0006/tr_0009 target FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision (leaf states, no children); inspection_equivalent_facts.states show these leaves have outgoing_transition_refs=[] (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING); the three region composites FrontendCollisionRegion/RearEndCollisionRegion/PedestrianCollisionRegion each have their own internal [*]->control edges but no incoming edge from the leaf states or from Inactive/ActiveState default entry, per inspection_equivalent_facts.states parent/outgoing fields and diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL.

binding_hints.reason: Inactive is the exact idle state from which the three collision-event transitions originate per exact_source_inventory tr_0003/tr_0006/tr_0009.

binding_hints.basis: NL3 quote: 'The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.'
binding_hints.reason: NL3 establishes that the active/operating behavior consists of concurrent activation of collision avoidance controls hosted in these three orthogonal region composites; the activation transition must therefore reach these region composites (or their owning ActiveState scope) to realize the described concurrent behavior.

binding_hints.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states entries for FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision showing outgoing_transition_refs=[] and reachable_from_initial=true while the corresponding region composites show reachable_from_initial=false
binding_hints.reason: These are the exact closed-model states actually reached by the activation transitions; they are dead-end leaves disconnected from the region composites, evidencing the wrong-target defect.

additional_contracts.normative_statement: Each of the three activation alternatives (frontend collision, rear-end collision, collision with pedestrian) from the inactive condition must reach the active/operating collision-avoidance region composite that performs the corresponding collision-avoidance control, not an isolated terminal placeholder disconnected from that control's orthogonal region.
additional_contracts.quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
additional_contracts.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine to become active (i.e., reach the operating collision-avoidance behavior, structurally the orthogonal regions described in NL3) upon each collision event. The closed FCSTM instead routes Inactive to three separate leaf states (FrontendCollision, RearEndCollision, PedestrianCollision) that have no outgoing edge into the corresponding region composites (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) which actually own the required Braking/Steering/EmergencyStop controls. This is a distinct wrong-target defect from the plain endpoint contract NL-CONTRACT-NL2-ENDPOINT-1 because it identifies the exact structural disconnection between the activation leaf and the region composite that must perform the concurrent control.
additional_contracts.scope: Activation transitions from Inactive to each collision-specific operating region

additional_contracts.normative_statement: The active mode of collision avoidance (ActiveState), which owns the three orthogonal regions required to concurrently activate the collision avoidance controls, must provide an exact default/owner-local entry path that reaches those region composites so the described concurrent behavior can occur.
additional_contracts.quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
additional_contracts.reason: ActiveState structurally owns the three orthogonal regions (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) that NL3 requires for concurrent activation of collision avoidance controls. The closed FCSTM's only default entry from ActiveState's initial pseudostate targets Inactive, and no transition from Inactive or elsewhere ever reaches these three region composites, so ActiveState lacks any exact default-entry path realizing the owned concurrent-region behavior described by NL3.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability of the three orthogonal collision-avoidance regions, reachable event-consumer coverage for Collision_Avoided, dead-end frontier facts for the three collision leaf states, and stable-termination/consequence properties of the activation transition group. The closed FCSTM shows FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion (and their child control states) are structurally present but unreachable_from_initial=false per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (all refuted reachability checks), because ActiveState only has an owner-local initial edge to Inactive, not to the three regions. I derive one additional reachability contract for the exact unreachable region scopes since this is a distinct root-reachability defect not captured by NL3's region_structure/state_action contracts (which describe structural existence/action retention, not reachability). I bind V1(initial_scope) for the leaf deadlock facts under the derived reachability obligation umbrella, since the collision leaves are dead ends given the broken return path. The cardinality contract NL-CONTRACT-REF-001 is bound to owner ActiveState/concurrent_regions per protocol; three region composites exist in inventory so binding is exact for domain, but this lens defers observed-count judgment to the deterministic frontier.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability of the three orthogonal collision-avoidance regions, reachable event-consumer coverage for Collision_Avoided, dead-end frontier facts for the three collision leaf states, and stable-termination/consequence properties of the activation transition group. The closed FCSTM shows FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion (and their child control states) are structurally present but unreachable_from_initial=false per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (all refuted reachability checks), because ActiveState only has an owner-local initial edge to Inactive, not to the three regions. This causes: (1) NL3 region_structure/state_action obligations to have unreachable concurrent controls, (2) NL2 event-consumer coverage for Collision_Avoided to fail reachable-consumer coverage even though it is declared, and (3) FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision are reachable leaves with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), a deadlock-frontier fact that, combined with the fact that the only way back to Inactive is through the now-unreachable region controls, exposes a broken response/consequence cycle. I derive one additional reachability contract for the exact unreachable region scopes since this is a distinct root-reachability defect not captured by NL3's region_structure/state_action contracts (which describe structural existence/action retention, not reachability). I bind V1(initial_scope) for the leaf deadlock facts under the derived reachability obligation umbrella, since the collision leaves are dead ends given the broken return path. The cardinality contract NL-CONTRACT-REF-001 is bound to owner ActiveState/concurrent_regions per protocol; three region composites exist in inventory so binding is exact for domain, but this lens defers observed-count judgment to the deterministic frontier.

issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the leaf states are merely intermediate 'signal' states that the diagram author intended without further behavior; but NL3 explicitly requires the regions to perform concurrent activation of controls, and a leaf with no continuation cannot realize any control activation, so this reading does not rebut the structural gap.
issues.title: Activation alternatives disconnect from the region composites required for concurrent collision-avoidance control

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text ActiveState block showing '[*] -> Inactive;' as the sole ActiveState-scoped initial edge; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for the three region composites; verify_facts refuted reachability checks for the same three composites.
issues.expected: ActiveState, as the owner of the three orthogonal regions performing concurrent collision-avoidance control, provides an exact reachable default-entry path into those regions.
issues.observed: ActiveState's own initial pseudostate edge ([*] -> Inactive) targets only Inactive; no other transition from ActiveState, Inactive, or the collision leaf states enters FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, or PedestrianCollisionRegion, so all three region composites and their child controls (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) remain unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: ActiveState is the exact owner of the region composites required by NL3 to perform concurrent control activation, but its only default entry targets Inactive; no edge realizes entry into the regions, leaving the owned concurrent-region behavior structurally unreachable from the owner's own scope.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each region composite does have its own internal initial edge ([*] -> BrakingControl, etc.), which could be read as satisfying 'initial entry' for that region in isolation; however this contract concerns ActiveState's owner-local entry into the regions themselves, which is a separate, unsatisfied obligation regardless of the regions' own internal entry edges.
issues.title: ActiveState lacks an owner-local default entry into its three orthogonal regions

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states (reachable_from_initial=false for the three regions and children); verify_facts.checks.non_proved reachability refuted rows for the same states; fcstm_model text showing ActiveState initial edge only targets Inactive.
issues.expected: While ActiveState is active, BrakingControl, SteeringControl, and EmergencyStop must be concurrently operating/activatable across the three orthogonal regions.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts show FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion and their child control states (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are reachable_from_initial=false / reachability refuted; ActiveState's only initial edge is [*]->Inactive, and Inactive's outgoing edges lead only to dead-end leaf states FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision with no outgoing transitions, never into the region composites.
issues.reason: state_action/progress retention has no frozen predicate expressing 'concurrently operating across unreachable regions'; the deterministic reachability facts show the controls can never actually run concurrently as required, which is a precise cross-view behavioral defect that must remain a W1 candidate rather than be silently dropped.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The regions and their control states are declared and structurally correct in the closed model; if a downstream mechanism (not captured in this finite graph) enters the regions concurrently with ActiveState's activation, the retention obligation could still be met, but no such entry edge exists in the supplied inventory.
issues.title: Concurrent collision-avoidance controls (BrakingControl, SteeringControl, EmergencyStop) are structurally present but unreachable, so the required concurrent operation cannot occur

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for Collision_Avoided (reachable_consumer_state_refs=[], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE; verify_facts.checks.non_proved event-consumer:Collision_Avoided refuted.
issues.expected: The sub-machine's activation and its response cycle require the Collision_Avoided event (emitted by BrakingControl/SteeringControl/EmergencyStop to return to Inactive) to have at least one reachable consumer, sustaining the activation/deactivation lifecycle implied by NL2.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers lists declared consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:12, transition:line:17, transition:line:22] for Collision_Avoided but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (empty); diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE confirms this; verify_facts.checks event-consumer:Collision_Avoided is refuted.
issues.reason: event_consumer_coverage has no frozen predicate for reachable-consumer-set comparison; declared-only presence cannot discharge the stronger reachable coverage property per lens priority, so this remains a precise W1 candidate distinct from the activation-event coverage which is satisfied (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian detected events are all reachably consumed at Inactive).
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL2 only explicitly requires activation-event coverage (frontend/rear-end/pedestrian detection), not the Collision_Avoided return event; one could argue Collision_Avoided coverage is out of NL2's exact scope. However, NL2 and NL3 together establish the sub-machine's activation/response lifecycle including collision avoidance controls, so the broken reachable consumer for the exit/avoidance event is a genuine behavioral consequence of the same activation scope.
issues.title: Collision_Avoided event has declared consumers but none is reachable, breaking the required return-to-inactive response coverage

issues.basis: verify_facts.checks.non_proved reachability entries (refuted) for FrontendCollisionRegion/RearEndCollisionRegion/PedestrianCollisionRegion; inspection_equivalent_facts.reachable_state_refs excludes these three composites; fcstm_model.text confirms no transition targets them.
issues.expected: FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, and PedestrianCollisionRegion must be reachable from the top-level initial entry so the concurrent collision-avoidance controls can actually activate as NL3 requires.
issues.observed: verify_facts.checks.non_proved contains refuted reachability results for state:FrontendCollisionRegion:line:9, state:BrakingControl:line:10, state:RearEndCollisionRegion:line:14, state:SteeringControl:line:15, state:PedestrianCollisionRegion:line:19, state:EmergencyStop:line:20, each with reachable_from_initial=false; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics confirms the same six STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL entries. ActiveState's sole initial edge (transition:line:31, [*]->Inactive) never enters the three region composites, and Inactive's outgoing edges (lines 32/33/34) target only the dead-end leaves FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision.
issues.reason: This is a finite path-existence/unreachable-target claim over the complete closed transition inventory, which G1 exactly expresses: no path exists from the root to any of the three orthogonal region composites.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The regions are correctly declared as children of ActiveState with valid internal [*]->control initial edges (transitions:line:11,16,21), so local structure is intact; one could argue root reachability of ActiveState itself (which is reachable) suffices for NL3's structural claim. But NL3's normative claim is about concurrent activation actually occurring, which requires the regions themselves to be entered, and no edge in the complete transition inventory enters them from anywhere reachable.
issues.title: The three orthogonal collision-avoidance regions are structurally declared but unreachable from the model root

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.states rows for the three regions (parent=ActiveState); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for the same regions; verify_facts.checks.non_proved reachability refuted.
issues.expected: ActiveState must provide orthogonal regions that structurally enable simultaneous activation of the different collision-avoidance controls (Braking, Steering, EmergencyStop).
issues.observed: The three region composites (FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion) are declared as children of ActiveState with internal initial edges to their respective control states, but none is reachable_from_initial per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts; the orthogonal structure exists syntactically but is operationally disconnected from ActiveState's actual behavior (ActiveState's only entry point is Inactive, and none of Inactive's dead-end successor leaves route into the regions).
issues.reason: region_structure has no frozen predicate; NL3's normative claim ties the orthogonal regions to actually 'allowing concurrent activation', so behavioral unreachability is evidence the structural obligation is not functionally realized, kept as a precise W1 candidate distinct from the narrower reachability contract which covers the pure path-existence property.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Declared composite containment (FrontendCollisionRegion/RearEndCollisionRegion/PedestrianCollisionRegion as children of ActiveState) is present in the exact source and closed-model inventories, which could be read as satisfying a purely structural region_structure obligation; the unreachability defect might belong solely to the derived reachability contract rather than duplicating here.
issues.title: Orthogonal regions exist structurally under ActiveState but are unreachable, undermining the required concurrent-activation structure

The closed FCSTM shows FrontendCollisionRegion, RearEndCollisionRegion, PedestrianCollisionRegion (and their child control states) are structurally present but unreachable_from_initial=false per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (all refuted reachability checks), because ActiveState only has an owner-local initial edge to Inactive, not to the three regions. This causes: (1) NL3 region_structure/state_action obligations to have unreachable concurrent controls, (2) NL2 event-consumer coverage for Collision_Avoided to fail reachable-consumer coverage even though it is declared, and (3) FrontendCollision/RearEndCollision/PedestrianCollision are reachable leaves with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), a deadlock-frontier fact that, combined with the fact that the only way back to Inactive is through the now-unreachable region controls, exposes a broken response/consequence cycle. I derive one additional reachability contract for the exact unreachable region scopes since this is a distinct root-reachability defect not captured by NL3's region_structure/state_action contracts (which describe structural existence/action retention, not reachability). I bind V1(initial_scope) for the leaf deadlock facts under the derived reachability obligation umbrella, since the collision leaves are dead ends given the broken return path. The cardinality contract NL-CONTRACT-REF-001 is bound to owner ActiveState/concurrent_regions per protocol; three region composites exist in inventory so binding is exact for domain, but this lens defers observed-count judgment to the deterministic frontier.
